A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Bayesian-LoRA and contain matching main sections and Appendices A–G. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of their equations, experiments, tables and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark, efficiency, ablation and distribution-shift experiments in Section 5, with additional Monte Carlo and Bayesian-optimization results in Appendices B and G.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and appendix results, including evaluations on commonsense reasoning, WikiText-2 and MATH.

M1.justification: The inducing-variable model, normalizing flow, ELBO, inference procedures and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The added attribution does not revise the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six commonsense benchmarks, WikiText-2, MATH and MMLU distribution-shift domains. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout, including Deep Ensembles in the efficiency comparison. Newly discussed FFG-U is cited as prior work but is not added to any experimental comparison.

E3.justification: Data splits, preprocessing, model backbones, metrics, early stopping, Monte Carlo evaluation settings and training configurations are unchanged. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: Flow-depth and inducing-size ablations, MAP recovery, distribution-shift tests, Monte Carlo sensitivity and Bayesian-optimization/Pareto analyses are retained unchanged, including their appendix evidence.

E5.justification: Statements about three seeds and existing mean ± standard deviation reporting are unchanged. Neither version adds different run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged, including Tables 1–9 and 14–16 and Figures 2–5. No result entries are added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: The definitions, propositions, deterministic-limit corollary, proofs and derivations are unchanged. Appendix A.3 adds a Ritter et al. citation while retaining the same ELBO equations and reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about the SGP–LoRA connection, flow-augmented inference, calibration, accuracy and computational overhead.

C2.justification: Interpretations of distribution-shift performance, accuracy–calibration trade-offs and Monte Carlo sampling are unchanged. The limitations concerning independent layer posteriors, applicability and theoretical bounds are also retained.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, prompting and preprocessing instructions, and hyperparameters remain unchanged, including Tables 11, 12 and 17. No code or data-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ritter et al. (2021), credits its FFG-U inducing-weight construction in Section 2, and cites it in Section 3.2 and Appendix A.3. Bibliography entries for Abbasi Yadkori et al. (2024) and Rajamohan et al. (2025) are removed. Broader positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 2 gains a short FFG-U explanation and a revised transition, alongside minor wording and date updates. Nearly all prose and the overall section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Added text changes column breaks and spacing on page 2, while bibliography edits reflow pages 9–11. Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–17 retain identical displays and captions.

improvement.justification: The FFG-U discussion and Ritter et al. citations clarify the stated provenance of the inducing-weight construction and ELBO derivation, providing a limited improvement in attribution. The new transition in Section 2 is grammatically awkward, but this small readability cost does not outweigh that benefit; scientific evidence remains unchanged.
